newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs rally on shortage on pipeline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs rally on shortage on pipeline.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices continued their rally in moderate midday trade on Friday with the Midwest soaring on forecasts for more cold weather and talk of propane shortages along a pipeline, players said.
The Cochin pipeline, which runs from Calgary, Canada, to parts of the upper Midwest, ran out of propane from between late Tuesday to late Thursday at its New Hampton, Iowa, terminal.
The terminal has a 20,000 barrel storage capacity.
"Most of our terminals are now full or close to full," said a Cochin official.
The shortage put upward pressure on Midwest prices and caused a quick run on wet barrels, traders said.
Forecasts for continued cold weather in the Midwest into next week also put pressure on propane as well as a draw in stocks in Thursday's Energy Information Administration report
The EIA reported a 1.1 million draw in the Midwest to 18.6 million barrels for the week ending Nov. 8.
Total U.S. stocks declined by 0.8 million, with a 200,000 barrel gain in the U.S. Gulf Coast and a 100,000 gain in the East, said the report.
In Conway, Kansas, hub spot propane traded at 61.00 cents, one cent above Thursday levels and any barrels were at 62.00 cents.
In Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot material rose about a half cent to between 57.00 cents and 57.25 cents.
Gasoline blending also put the pressure on normal butane, which rose 2.50 cents in Belvieu and 0.75 cent in Conway.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
